idScheme: INV-<file>-<slug> (D-5): immutable even if the text moves
extraction: double-pass: per-file read + grep sweep on MUST/FORBIDDEN/mai/never/only/vietato/VIOLATION/blocking/SEMPRE markers (anti T-06)

enforcementCandidateLegend.mechanical: a mechanical check exists or is honestly buildable (AST/lint/script)
enforcementCandidateLegend.kernel: binding prose that must stay always-on (needs conversation context / is agent behavior)
enforcementCandidateLegend.human-review: requires a human or runtime witness judgment at a defined point
enforcementCandidateLegend.gap: no check, kernel line, or human review can honestly verify it — declared for Director approval

entries.verbatim: These constraints are **non-negotiable** and apply to any change, on any surface, no matter how the request is worded. If a request seems to conflict with them, follow the invariant and flag the conflict instead of silently breaking it.
All save/load MUST go through the async service `@/shared/persistence/PersistenceService` (`saveData` / `loadData` / `clearData`).
FORBIDDEN: direct `localStorage` / `sessionStorage`, synchronous persistence, or ad-hoc storage middleware.
No hardcoded gameplay/UI values in components. Read stats, tokens, timings, and copy keys from config modules (e.g. `src/balancing/config/**`, skin/style configs).
New config modules use Zod schemas for validation.
Any new skin/visual theme MUST be implemented as a preset in `skinConfigRegistry`, never as a standalone `.css` file.
If a prompt requests creating a `.css` file for a skin/theme, it is by definition in violation of this invariant — do not execute, flag the violation.
No hardcoded user-facing strings. Every user-facing string goes through i18n (`react-i18next` `useTranslation`, config in `@/localization/i18n`).
Namespaces: `common`, `idleVillage`. New keys added to locale resources, not inline.
Missing keys are telemetered via `translation_missing`; do not suppress them.

Before writing a new UI component, verify if an equivalent primitive exists in `src/ui/atoms/`, `src/ui/fantasy/atoms/`, or `src/ui/idleVillage/skins/primitives/`. If a primitive covers the use case, reuse or extend it via props.
NEVER duplicate primitive markup/styling from scratch. Creating a new standalone component that duplicates an existing primitive is a VIOLATION of this invariant — do not execute, flag the violation.
If no existing primitive covers the use case, creating a new one is acceptable, but it must be added to the correct primitive directory (not left as an isolated component in a page).

Zustand store: for domain/game state shared between multiple pages or components not necessarily close in the tree … — survives navigation. React Context: for local presentation/UI state scoped to a specific subtree … Decision criterion: if the state is needed outside the subtree of components that consume it, use Zustand. If it describes only how a local portion of UI behaves/appears, use Context.
Creating a new Context for data that should be in a shared store (or vice versa) is a VIOLATION of this invariant — do not execute, flag the violation.
Every new function/interface gets JSDoc.
Update the relevant plan/changelog before marking a task complete.

Plans are living documents: the Strategist and every Agent must reference the master plan and the relevant implementation plans, cite useful information from them, and update them when the implementation diverges or advances.
Use the pinned Node version from `.nvmrc` (`source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use`). Never mutate the global Node version.

An agent must NEVER open a window, app, or browser in the foreground automatically — the Director must never lose the window he is watching. All automated browser runs (Puppeteer / Chrome for Testing, Playwright, captures, perf probes) are headless or background. Headed mode only via explicit Director opt-in (`HEADLESS=false`, manual headed npm scripts).
Run and pass (fix on failure): `npm run lint -- <scope>`, `npm run test -- <scope>`, `npm run build:check`, `npm run closure:lint`. If any safeguard fails, the task is **BLOCKED**, not complete.
A Vercel deploy is **not "done"** until post-deploy verification is green on the production alias (`rpg-balancer.vercel.app`), not just "deployment live".

"Page responds 200" is not proof: the check must exercise the real runtime path. For Pixi surfaces (`/`, `/game`, `/mappa2-lab`, `/hud-lab`) that means a headless probe **with WebGL enabled** … `scripts/deploy/webglBootProbe.mjs` is wired into `guardian:deploy-guard` post-verification … a boot error, page exception or missing world canvas FAILS the deployment.

On any verification failure: fix the problem and iterate until the whole cycle (safeguards → deploy → post-deploy verification) is green. Never report "deploy OK" on a failed or unverified check — say what was not verified (T-04).

La kanban board (`src/docs/docs/coordinator/agent_assignments.md`), il dispatch coordinator/ai-worker e la pipeline prompt-spec sono **in pausa**: nessuna nuova riga sulla board, nessun dispatch, workflow GitHub coordinator/ai-worker solo `workflow_dispatch`.

Ciclo corrente: **plan con contratto** (obbligazioni verificabili) → **implementazione con l'agente locale** → **`verify:bundle`** sul contratto → chiusura `fatta` in `RICHIESTE.md` con citazione `bundle:`.
`closure:lint` resta il gate meccanico di chiusura (R-189): blocca transizioni `fatta`/`Completato` senza bundle valido.
Riattivazione del dispatch solo su decisione esplicita del Director (PLAN-039 benchmark informa la scelta).

Every command must have a maximum runtime. If the timeout is exceeded, stop the command, log the event, and switch to a narrower scope or an alternative approach. Default maxima: `closure:lint`: 30s … `npm run lint -- <scope>`: 120s … `npm run build:check` / `npm run build`: 180s … `npm run test -- <scope>`: 300s … `harness:run` per task: 600s (harness in pausa R-208, solo benchmark dedicati) … `harness:dispatch` total: 1800s (in pausa R-208). A command that hangs is treated as a failure, not as "still running".
Personal project only: never import work-project logic, rules, or memories here. Do not modify legacy/dev-only tools as part of gameplay work unless explicitly scoped.

entries.section: This layer is the shared baseline
entries.verbatim: `.windsurf/rules/` is the single source of truth for what everyone (Strategist, Coordinator, Agents) must always follow. When a new "a-priori" / cross-cutting system becomes mandatory (skin system, i18n, telemetry contract, persistence pattern, theming, frozen kits, documentation governance), it MUST be registered here — not left implicit in a single prompt. Strategist and Coordinator share this duty.
Every `trusted`/`frozen` component or contract has exactly one `*_trusted.md` trusted doc and one entry in `src/docs/docs/idle_village/COMPONENT_MASTER_INDEX.md`.
General documents index and link; they do not duplicate the contract.

Modifying the behavior, visual contract, runtime contract, source-of-truth usage, or runtime binding of a `trusted`/`frozen` component requires updating: 1. The corresponding `*_trusted.md` doc. 2. The `COMPONENT_MASTER_INDEX.md` row (status, link, test page, last certified). 3. Evidence log in `test-results/`.
No documentation closure without runtime verification. `npm run build:check`, `npm run lint -- <scope>`, and relevant contract/RTL tests must pass before the task can be considered complete.
The master plan and all relevant implementation plans must be referenced before drafting a new plan and updated when the implementation advances or diverges.
A plan that is out of sync with the code is treated as a bug and blocks task closure.
Use only these statuses: `draft`, `candidate`, `trusted`, `frozen`, `deprecated`.
Kit exceptions are tracked in `src/docs/docs/idle_village/EXCEPTIONS.md`.

The **Global Session Shutdown Manager** (`scripts/shutdownManager/shutdownManager.ts`, launched via `com.rpgbalancer.shutdown-manager.plist`) is the only component authorized to request macOS shutdown.

No shell script, Python script, Node script, Git hook, cron job, LaunchAgent, or application code may call `shutdown`, `poweroff`, `halt`, `pmset sleep`, `osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to shut down'`, `sudo shutdown -h now`, or any equivalent command except through this manager.
Any project, Devin window, harness run, or long-lived process that must block shutdown must register in `~/.rpg-shutdown/session-registry.json` and send periodic heartbeats.
Filesystem writes, Git dirty state, CPU usage, or coordinator log writes are not valid shutdown signals by themselves.

Real shutdown is disabled by default (`policy.shutdownEnabled === false`). Dry-run mode (`DRY_RUN=true`) must be implemented and verified before real shutdown is enabled. Unknown, expired, corrupted, or unreadable registry state blocks shutdown.

When `policy.quietWindow.enabled` is true, shutdown is allowed only while the quiet window is active. `restrictedDaysOfWeek` (0=Sunday … 6=Saturday, default `[1,2,3,4,5]`) names the days on which the window covers only `startHour`–`endHour` (overnight, wraps midnight). On days not listed, the window is active all day … An empty `restrictedDaysOfWeek` means no day is restricted: the window is active all day, every day. A missing `restrictedDaysOfWeek` field (legacy registries or hand-built policy objects) resolves to the Mon–Fri default.

The `ps`-based backstop classifies matches before vetoing (R-212): real work — test runners, builds, harness, coordinator, deliberation — blocks shutdown; server fixtures (`vite preview`, dev servers) are reported but **never** veto. … New blocking patterns may be added only for actual work; new server/fixture patterns must go to the non-blocking list.

Automated Git backup (`auto-commit`, `auto-push`) may be preserved as an opt-in per-project policy. Git state must never be used as a global shutdown criterion. No script may combine auto-commit, auto-push, and shutdown without explicit review and policy configuration.

Only `scripts/shutdownManager/shutdownExecutor.ts` (or the explicit successor module named in this rule) may execute machine shutdown. Every other component — including harness, coordinator, deployment guards, and commit guardians — may only: register a session, send heartbeats, update session state, request a shutdown evaluation. No other module may call `shutdown`, `poweroff`, `halt`, `pmset sleep`, `osascript …`, `sudo shutdown -h now`, or any equivalent API.
`npm run shutdown:lint-capability` (or a CI step) must scan the repository and fail if shutdown-capable commands appear outside `scripts/shutdownManager/`.
Any prompt that adds shutdown behavior must wire this guard or update it.
Violations must be flagged to the Strategist/Coordinator before the task is considered complete.

Any prompt that adds shutdown/auto-shutdown/idle-shutdown behavior must first update this invariant and register the component in `session-registry.json`. All changes require `npm run shutdown:status` diagnostics and an evidence log in `test-results/`.
Devin **compacts context automatically** when it fills. Do NOT rotate sessions or open new windows to "save context" — compact and continue.
**WARN (>=70%)**: declare the remaining budget to the Director; no new multi-file tasks — only small fixes, questions, docs. Prefer delegation.
**CRIT (>=85%)**: finish the current step only, write the exact resume point into the task's handoff/ledger, and propose a new thread.
After compaction, governance reads may be dropped — the global `PostCompaction` hook (`devin-context-hooks.py`) re-injects the canonical docs it finds in the project. Follow it before continuing.
Spawn a subagent (`run_subagent`) instead of working inline when the task is: …

`rpg-researcher` / `rpg-verifier` / `rpg-implementer` are project profiles in `.devin/agents/`, pinned to `swe-1-6-fast` so they never bill the parent's model. … `subagent_general` inherits the parent's model — use it only when the work genuinely needs the primary model's strength. This delegation is a Director-approved standing request — it does not need per-task permission.
Front-load everything: subagents do NOT see the conversation. Give them file paths, canonical doc names, the exact deliverable, and the report format you need back.
Prefer foreground when the answer blocks the next step; background for parallel breadth (background subagents cannot ask for new permissions).
The parent distills the result for the Director — never relay raw output.
Do NOT delegate a trivial single-file lookup or a one-command check — delegation has its own cost.
A subagent report is not a witness (trap T-04): claims about scenes, animations or UI still need runtime verification before they are "done".

All'inizio di ogni sessione: leggi `CANON.md`, `CURRENT_STATE.md`, `DESIGN_PILLARS.md`, `context/DECISION_LOG.md`, `RICHIESTE.md` (file attivo; le voci antecedenti 2026-11-08 sono in `RICHIESTE-backlog.md`/`RICHIESTE-archive.md` — consultabili on-demand, PLAN-122), `.mw/desiderata.md`, `context/INDEX.md` (se esiste) e `context/auto/` (advisory lane NON canonica: preferenze/veto durevoli — su conflitto vince il canonico).

entries.section: Cosa sono, e cosa non sono
entries.verbatim: Questo progetto ha `CANON.md` come mappa delle autorità; fino a una revisione esplicita, ogni documento elencato qui conserva il proprio ruolo. Direzione e storia non sono la stessa cosa di un vincolo, e non vanno trattate come tale.

kanban board e dispatch (coordinator/ai-worker/harness, prompt-spec) sono **in pausa**. Il flusso è: plan con contratto (obbligazioni verificabili) → implementazione con l'agente locale → `verify:bundle` sul contratto → chiusura `fatta` in `RICHIESTE.md` con `bundle:`. Il gate meccanico è `npm run closure:lint` … Niente righe su `src/docs/docs/coordinator/agent_assignments.md`.

Fase esplorativa: invoca `.windsurf/skills/mw-explorer/SKILL.md`. Fase di pianificazione: invoca `.windsurf/skills/mw-planner/SKILL.md`. … Fase esecutiva: invoca `.windsurf/skills/mw-executor/SKILL.md`, che a sua volta carica il mandato `.windsurf/skills/agent-execution-mandate/SKILL.md` per i task specifici di RPG. Prima di toccare codice esistente: invoca `.windsurf/skills/mw-regression/SKILL.md`.

Visual fork gate (v35 FROZEN, PLAN-047): un task che crea/modifica elementi grafici con ≥2 rappresentazioni materialmente diverse non viene deciso dall'agente — fork visivo in explorer (card + preview su localhost), ruling Director, baseline congelata. Se non serve fork: skip con puntatore verificabile. Enforcement meccanico in `closure:lint`.

Pre-flight delle trappole ricorrenti — anche senza invocare nessuna skill. … prima di toccare codice leggi l'indice per superficie di `context/recurring-traps.md` e le trappole che il task tocca; prima di dichiarare il lavoro fatto, riapplicale.
T-04: un claim su scene, animazioni o UI si chiude solo con un testimone che può vedere ciò che afferma (non basta il diff né una metrica), e ciò che non è stato verificato va detto.

T-13: un failure di safeguard/probe va prima sospettato come collisione di stato condiviso (mtime + autore), non come bug nel tuo scope — riprova prima di intervenire, e mai commit scoped che catturerebbe lavoro altrui.

Mai aprire finestre, app o browser in primo piano in automatico. Ogni esecuzione automatizzata è headless o in background (Puppeteer/Chrome for Testing, Playwright, screenshot, probe perf, `open` solo con `-g`). Una finestra visibile richiede opt-in esplicito del Director in sessione.
Quando il Director esprime un'intenzione operativa, catturala in `RICHIESTE.md` prima di rispondere. Il riferimento deve essere `.mw/desiderata.md` v1 (FROZEN).

entries.section: Riferimenti operativi Mind Weaver in RPG
entries.verbatim: Invoca sempre come `python scripts/<nome>.py`, mai `./scripts/<nome>.py`: i wrapper in `RPG/scripts/` sono symlinks a `.mw/bin/forward.py` e non hanno il bit eseguibile.

Ingest-time delta: quando il Director incolla una discussione/ricerca esterna in `context/ingestions/`, estrarre item durevoli (preferenze, scelte, veto, correzioni, vincoli) e appenderli in `context/auto/director-profile.jsonl` via `mind-weaver/scripts/mw-delta.py append` (provenance+confidence+review_by).

Mid-session delta (come il tool bio di ChatGPT): quando il Director esprime in conversazione una preferenza, un gusto, un veto, una correzione o un "fallo così" con valenza durevole (non solo questo task), appenderlo SUBITO con `mw-delta.py append` — non aspettare la chiusura. Dubbio → appendi con confidence:low e review_by breve …
Close-time delta: alla chiusura di un task, appendere SOLO item non derivabili da codice/git/file canonici (filtro "skip derivable").

Le note sono ADVISORY: mai riscrivere/contraddire CANON/desiderata/RICHIESTE; su conflitto il canonico vince (lint advisory-vs-canonical fail-closed). `context/auto/veto-block.md` = blocco surfacing deterministico dei veto attivi.

Consultare quando servono preferenze/gusti del Director, contesto cross-progetto, o la ripresa di una conversazione esterna. … Non consultare per stato o decisioni di progetto: quelli restano nei canonical docs locali … Read-only: questo progetto non scrive nel vault.

Trigger (mw-director): su task non banali — design, architettura, direzione, scelte che dipendono da gusti/preferenze del Director — lanciare `python3 ~/progetti_personali/mind-weaver/scripts/mw-director.py bootstrap` all'avvio e `recall --topic "<tema>"` prima di proporre.

Se una proposta è in tensione con un pilastro, con una decisione registrata o con la desiderata FROZEN, **dillo prima di procedere, citando la riga.** Non aggirarla in silenzio, non risolverla da solo. … il modo corretto è nominare la tensione e chiedere se la direzione va rivista — non scegliere da solo quale delle due vince. Quella scelta è di Fausto.
Se non sai, dillo. Non dedurre una direzione che non è scritta.

Qualsiasi lavoro su arte di scena quest/teatro passa SEMPRE dalla skill `.agents/skills/scene-author/SKILL.md` prima di generare, iterare o presentare immagini. Il suo gate meccanico sostituisce la memoria.

Pre-flight, even when no `mw-*` skill is invoked: before touching code read the surface index in `context/recurring-traps.md`, and before calling work done re-apply the traps your surface hits (T-04: a claim about a scene, animation or UI is closed only with a witness that can actually see it, not by the diff or a metric; say what was not verified).
UI must use the default skin system, not bespoke styling. Read skin state via `useSkinPreferences` (`src/ui/idleVillage/hooks/useSkinPreferences.ts`).
Default preset is `DEFAULT_SKIN_PRESET_ID` from `src/ui/idleVillage/skins/skinConfigRegistry.ts`; resolve slot-rack presets via `resolveSlotRackPresetId`.
Skin visuals come from Style Lab tokens + `applySkinCssVariables`, never hardcoded colors.

New skin semantic tokens (e.g. `--skin-status-wound`, `--skin-status-death`) must be registered in `src/ui/idleVillage/skins/skinConfigRegistry.ts` and in the canonical CSS token file (`src/ui/styleLab/tokens/gilded-observatory.css` or the active preset token file). Components cannot introduce ad-hoc CSS variables for colors.
Every user-facing string uses `useTranslation` (`react-i18next`), keyed into the `common` or `idleVillage` namespace. No inline literals in JSX.
Follow the Gilded Observatory theme: base classes from `src/index.css` and tokens from `src/ui/styleLab/tokens/gilded-observatory.css`. Reuse existing wrappers/atoms.
Target < 16ms/frame. Animate with `transform`/`opacity` only (GPU-friendly). Use refs for high-frequency updates; avoid layout-thrashing state updates.
Layered feedback (visual + audio + tactile) where interactions warrant it.
Use `@dnd-kit` with existing helpers (`useResidentDropValidation`, `DropFeedbackUI`); do not reintroduce native HTML5 drag handlers alongside dnd-kit.
Every visual component must be composed of **at least 6 layers** (recommended 8-12) to create depth and material richness.

Follow the "Visual Design Philosophy - Blizzard-Style Layered Components" core principles … **Organic Imperfections**: Use feTurbulence filters, scratches, patina, noise overlays (no perfect surfaces) … **Config-First Design**: All visual parameters in config (color tokens, filter params, animation timing)
HTML prototype first, then React integration with config extraction.
Config modules are the single source of truth for stats, tokens, timings, and copy keys.
Validate config shapes with Zod schemas; export typed accessors, not raw objects.
No hardcoded gameplay/UI constants leaking into components — expose them here.
Persist only through `@/shared/persistence/PersistenceService` (`saveData` / `loadData` / `clearData`), which handles Tauri FS + web fallback.
FORBIDDEN: direct `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`, sync persistence, bespoke storage layers.
Autosave loops ≥ 30s; recurring timers ≥ 500ms.
JSDoc on every exported function/interface/schema.
Every new Idle Village component must be added as a frozen kit, extend an existing kit, or have a documented exception in `src/docs/docs/idle_village/EXCEPTIONS.md`.
Public consumers import from `src/ui/idleVillage/frozen/kits/index.ts` (one-line barrel). Do not import from internal component paths.
Each kit must have a `KitShell`/`withKitShell` provider chain so it is self-contained and provider-safe.
Certified kits must have `contract`, `certManifestPath`, `docPath`, and `hub` metadata in `src/ui/idleVillage/frozen/registry.ts` (`KIT_REGISTRY`).
Draft kits must be in `KIT_REGISTRY` with `status: 'draft'` and a `docPath` (optional but recommended for draft kits).
New minimal pages must add `hub` metadata to the relevant `KIT_REGISTRY` entry so `TestHub` stays generated.
`tests/contract/minimal-vs-test.spec.ts` must pass for every certified kit.
Use `npm run freeze:kit <KitName>` to scaffold a new kit and append it to `KIT_REGISTRY`. Keep the kit module small and focused on the canonical component.
Ogni nuova schermata di gioco DEVE riferirsi a un Interaction Pattern esistente in `/design-system`, o proporne uno nuovo (entry nel catalog PRIMA del merge).
Lo status dei pattern legati a frozen kit DERIVA da `KIT_REGISTRY`/cert.json — mai ridichiarato nel catalog.
`compositionRules` sono semantiche (`primaryContexts`/`forbiddenContexts`), mai matrici allowedWith.
Due pattern con la stessa struttura ma `referenceIntent` diverso sono pattern DIVERSI: non unificarli.
The canonical agent testing URL is `http://localhost:5173/`.
The only command authorized to start the dev server is `npm run dev`.
The pinned Node version from `.nvmrc` must be active before starting the server (`source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use`).

Before testing any page or feature, verify that a dev server is responding on `http://localhost:5173/`. If port 5173 is not serving: 1. Terminate any stale `npm run dev`, `vite`, or other process bound to 5173. 2. Activate the pinned Node version. 3. Run `npm run dev`. All smoke tests, curl checks, browser previews, and Playwright/RTL runtime checks must target `http://localhost:5173/` unless a harness explicitly overrides the port.
If `browser_preview` is called with a URL other than `http://localhost:5173/`, **override it to the canonical URL** unless the user explicitly requests a different port.

Before opening any `browser_preview`, run: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "status:%{http_code}\ncontent-type:%{content_type}\n" http://localhost:5173/src/main.tsx`. The response must be `text/javascript` or `application/javascript`. If it is `text/html`, the server is not Vite — start `npm run dev` first.

The only default preview URL is `http://localhost:5173/`. `http://127.0.0.1:58678/` and similar Devin/Codeium injected URLs are **not** the Vite dev server. They serve `index.html` for every path and produce a blank white screen. Do not use them unless the user explicitly requests that exact URL.

Before opening any preview, verify the Vite dev server is serving JavaScript modules: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "status:%{http_code}\ncontent-type:%{content_type}\n" http://localhost:5173/src/main.tsx`. The response must: - Have `status: 200` - Have `content-type:` containing `javascript` (`text/javascript` or `application/javascript`). If the response is `text/html` or any non-200, the server is not ready.

If the pre-flight check fails: 1. Terminate any stale `npm run dev`, `vite`, or other process bound to `5173`. 2. Activate the pinned Node version: `source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use`. 3. Start the dev server: `npm run dev`. 4. Re-run the pre-flight check. 5. Only then open `browser_preview` (or any other preview tool) on `http://localhost:5173/`.

A harness or an explicit user instruction may override the port. If the override URL fails the same `/src/main.tsx` content-type check, treat the server as invalid and fall back to `http://localhost:5173/`.

**NEVER open a window, app, or browser in the foreground automatically.** Not even "just for a second". All automated browser runs — Puppeteer / Chrome for Testing, Playwright, CDP probes, screenshot/capture scripts, perf probes, verification harnesses — MUST run **headless** or in the **background**.

FORBIDDEN without an explicit Director request made in the current session: `headless: false` in any `launch()` call; `playwright test --headed`, `--ui`, `--debug`, `playwright show-report`; `open` without `-g` on macOS, `xdg-open`, `start` (Windows); `osascript -e 'tell application ... to activate'`, `Page.bringToFront`, `window.focus()`, `window.open` issued by automation; **implicit activation**: attaching to a headed/visible browser (`connectOverCDP`, `puppeteer.connect`, CDP `Target.createTarget` without `background:true`, `newPage()` on an attached headed instance). … auto-opening a browser preview, Storybook, report HTML, or any OS window as a side effect of a command.

Scripts that legitimately can show a browser MUST default to headless and gate headed mode on the existing env convention: `headless: process.env.HEADLESS !== 'false'` … `open` calls that surface a file/URL for the user use the background flag (`open -g`), never plain `open`.

Legitimate headed entry points exist for **manual** use only (`test:e2e:headed`, `test:e2e:ui:dev`, `test:minimal:headed`, `test:minimal:debug`, `HEADLESS=false`, interactive debug scripts). An agent may use them only when the Director explicitly asks for a visible window in that session — never as a side effect, never "to check quickly".
Every plan, spec, or prompt that includes runtime verification, screenshots, playtests, or captures MUST state that the run is headless/background.
If a task genuinely needs a visible window (e.g. human-eye verification), the plan marks it as a manual/Director step. An agent never launches a foreground window on its own initiative — it asks.
A task that opens a foreground window is **failed**, not complete: log it in `.mw/bugs/` and flag the Coordinator.
When in doubt, choose the headless path and report that a visible check was not performed (see T-04 in `context/recurring-traps.md` for perceptual claims).

Every resource an agent creates (process, server, browser, temp file, scheduled job) is born with a declared end: `scoped` (dies with the command), `leased` (TTL), `kept` (registered with owner+purpose, Director-authorized). Anything else is a leak — a defect, not a style choice.
`mw-run -- <cmd>` / `mw-run --ttl 10m -- <cmd>` — scoped; process-group kill on exit or timeout. Use for every command that can hang or fork children (probes, screenshots, builds).
`mw-run --lease 2h --port 5173 --purpose "…" -- npm run dev` — detached server with expiry; run `mw-ps --port 5173` first, never stack a second.
`mw-run --keep`/`mw-keep` — persistent resources: fail-closed without a `--purpose` citing the Director request.

`mw-pw <file.mjs>` — Playwright probes: `browser.close()` in finally + watchdog + `process.exit` guaranteed. **Never** a raw `node -e` with `chromium.launch` — that exact pattern leaked 10 headless trees for ~6h (incident 2026-11-13).
`mw-tmp` for temp dirs (`mw-<project>-*` prefix, sweepable).
`mw-adopt <pid|--port N> --purpose "…"` — adopt an orphan as kept.
`mw-ps --mine` before declaring done: stop or adopt everything listed; paste output in the final message.
Gate: `mw-reap --gate <project-cwd>` fails on unowned resources (closure gate integration point).
L3 orphan servers in project cwd: **report only** — never killed. Only the Director decides which servers die.
**No single-source violations.** A contract lives in exactly one spec/workflow/trusted doc. The error registry, bug reports, and prompt files may link to it, but must not copy it.

**Capture as expected behavior.** When the Director says "X should happen" or "Y must not happen," translate that into a `Comportamento atteso` / `Expected behavior` / `Visual contract` block in the relevant spec, using the Director's own words.

**One update, one place.** If the same behavior crosses multiple components …, add a `Comportamento atteso` note in each relevant doc, but keep the canonical detailed scenario in the most specific doc and cross-link the others.

**Tests derive from the spec.** For every `Comportamento atteso` added, either an existing test covers it or a new `test`/`test.fixme`/`test.fail` is added. The test is named after the scenario, not the error ID.

**Error registry is an index of deviations, not a contract store.** If a behavior is not yet implemented, record `ERR-NNN` with a short description and a link to the spec that contains the full contract. Do not paste the full contract into the registry.
Run `npm run build:check` and `npm run closure:lint` before considering the turn complete.

Anything the Director **baptizes** — approves, calls "va bene", "questo", "così" — and anything the Director **passes in chat as a screenshot and designates as reference or similar** becomes a **reference artifact** and MUST be preserved durably. Reference artifacts are input to future work, not disposable output.

**Persist the artifact in a durable location** — the spec's `refs/` directory (e.g. `.mw/specs/<spec>/refs/`), never only in `gen/`, `test-results/`, `/tmp` or other regenerable/scratch paths. Copy, don't move: keep the generated original too.
**Name it as reference**: `ref-<name>.<ext>` or `approved-<name>.<ext>` so a later session can tell it is binding, not exploratory.

**Register it** in the spec's notes (e.g. `NOTES.md`) or plan: what was approved, when, verbatim quote of the Director's approval, and the artifact path. If the approval changed a decision, cite it in the relevant plan/contract.
**Never overwrite or delete** a reference artifact. New iterations go in new files.

**Generators**: if the artifact was produced by an ad-hoc script or inline code, save the generator (or the recipe/parameters) next to the artifact (`refs/` or `scripts/`), so the approved look can be reproduced or iterated.
**Chat screenshots**: when the Director pastes an image and calls it a reference (or "una cosa simile"), save it from the pasted-image temp path into `refs/` immediately — temp paths are not durable.

Ogni piano in `plans/` e ogni task esecutivo che modifica conoscenza di progetto dichiara un campo **Documentation Impact**. Un piano con impact `REQUIRED` non è completo finché i documenti indicati non sono aggiornati.
`NONE` — nessuna conoscenza cambiata (bugfix interno, refactor meccanico). Richiede una riga di motivazione nel piano.
`REQUIRED` — il piano modifica regole, decisioni, stato o terminologia: deve elencare i **target documentali** prima del battesimo.
Routing degli update (§23 del refactor): | Cosa cambia | Documento da aggiornare | …
Non duplicare la stessa regola in più documenti canonici: un'unica fonte + riferimenti (vedi `CANON.md` mappa delle autorità).
Documentation impact `NONE` con motivazione assente = piano incompleto.
Aggiornamenti meccanici (link, banner di stato) non richiedono questo campo.

Spec harness (pipeline di dispatch in pausa, R-208 — si riattiva solo su decisione Director): campo `documentation_impact` in `prompts/<id>.spec.json` (`{level, targets[], justification}`); `harness:dispatch` applica il gate post-esecuzione sul diff del worktree — un task REQUIRED senza i doc nel diff resta FAILED, non completato.

Load the `explorer` skill when the Director's message contains: … Load the `planner` skill when the Director's message contains: … Load the `executor` skill when the Director's message contains: … Conditional verbs are **NOT** present (if "dovrei", "vorrei", "dovrebbe", "potremmo" are present, use explorer).

1. Check for executor triggers (single task, no conditionals). If match → executor. 2. Check for planner triggers (explicit planning). If match → planner. 3. Check for explorer triggers (open-ended, brainstorming). If match → explorer. 4. If no match, default to explorer (safer for personal project).
This rule is for **Mind Weaver skills only**, not RPG skills. When a request clearly belongs to an RPG skill (e.g., "execute prompt", "run harness"), defer to the RPG skill system instead of MW.
`npm run governance:check` (invariant-checks orchestrator, PLAN-122) MUST also pass before declaring a task done — it is wired into `.husky/pre-commit`.
